answers.solution:
## Diagnosis

gitreins tier1 (`go_tests` guard) FAILED on a commit whose own tests were green, with the tell-tale line `? <module>/cmd/gendocs [no test files]` quoted as the failure. Root cause was NOT the code: a sibling lane (releng) had left an UNCOMMITTED extra line on the shared git-tracked board (.coding-hermes/board/tasks.jsonl), and the line was malformed JSON — it carried a stray `RELEASE-006|` prefix before the JSON object. TestCHT058BoardIDIntegrity (the board id-integrity gate, CHT-058) reads the on-disk board, so it failed on the sibling's dirty state, and tier1 grades `go test ./...`, so the failure surfaced as an unrelated package's `[no test files]` line. Cost: two judge artifacts (c1d65606, 1dd0155a) burned as tier1 FAIL on the same foreign cause.

## Fix (three steps)

- **A. Prove the cause is foreign, not yours** — the judge's criterion text names the failing test; run that one test yourself and read its message (it named the malformed line and the file). `git status` shows the sibling's uncommitted board edit.
- **B. Repair byte-preserving, do not revert** — the sibling lane was already dead (no live process), and its row was complete and correct except for the prefix: strip the stray prefix, validate every line with json.loads, assert the id list is stable, numstat must show 1 added line (not a whole-file rewrite), then `make board-gate` (15 self-test checks + shipped-board parse) must pass.
- **C. Re-judge after the tree is clean** — tier1 grades the LIVE workdir, so re-dispatch `judge --async`; the re-run passed tier1+tier2 (bbff5623). Record the failed artifacts as superseded on the board row, never as evidence.

## General rule

On a repo whose board/.gitreins state is shared by concurrent lanes, a tier1 go_tests FAIL that your own `go test ./...` does not reproduce means FOREIGN WORKING-TREE STATE, first suspect a sibling's uncommitted file, second your own harness seams — re-run the named test and read its message before touching code.

Tier 2 may still return COMPLETE (its criterion is the row's work); only tier1 blocks.
